articles.summary: OpenAI is sunsetting its AI-powered browser after less than a year. But it's moving some agentic browsing features to its desktop app and a Chrome extension.

articles.title: New York Times says OpenAI hid evidence in ChatGPT copyright trial
articles.summary: News publishers say OpenAI hid tools and datasets that could identify copyrighted journalism in ChatGPT outputs, escalating their lawsuit with a new motion for sanctions.

articles.title: Google will now disclose which ads are made with AI
articles.summary: While Google prohibits misleading and deceptive ads, an ad can still leverage AI to create some type of synthetic or digitally altered content. Until now, that's something Google only required election ads to disclose.

articles.title: Instagram users: Here’s how to stop Meta’s AI from using your photos
articles.summary: Muse Image allows users to generate AI images using photos from public Instagram accounts. As long as a person's profile is public, another user can tag that account and use their images as part of an AI-generated creation.

articles.title: Meta’s new AI chips will begin production in September

articles.title: What can best ease transmission bottlenecks? More transfer capacity, DOE says.
articles.summary: Transmission congestion added $12 billion in wholesale power costs in 2024, the U.S. Department of Energy said in a draft report on U.S. transmission needs.

articles.title: New York reaches 8 GW of distributed solar capacity
articles.summary: Tony Smith, chair of the Virginia Distributed Solar Alliance, told Utility Dive that other states can learn from New York’s policies that “reduce soft costs, provide investment certainty, and remove utility-specific interconnection barriers.”

articles.title: KKR to buy EDF power solutions’ North American operations for $4.2B
articles.summary: EDF power solutions owns and runs a portfolio of solar, wind and battery storage assets across multiple regions. The company said its U.S. and Canada operations serve a wide range of utilities, companies and institutional customers.

articles.title: Duke reduces rate hike request, still faces regulator pushback
articles.summary: The utility dropped its proposed residential rate increase to 11.6% from 18% after pushback, but hearings this week highlighted continued unease. “I don't see how you can say that we're benefiting customers,” one utility commissioner said.

articles.title: PJM status quo ‘untenable’: FERC Commissioner LaCerte
articles.summary: “Looking at things differently is hard, especially in entrenched utilities that have been doing this for a long time,” the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission member said.

articles.title: DOE closes up to $3.26B loan to AEP Texas
articles.summary: The money is intended to go toward upgrading and building transmission lines spanning roughly 2,800 miles. The utility has agreements supporting up to 41 GW of potential new load.

articles.title: Illinois regulators approve ComEd VPP under new clean energy law
articles.summary: The program will discharge power from small batteries during events like the early-July heatwave that pushed PJM Interconnection demand to near-record levels.

articles.title: IRA clean energy gains mostly on track despite OBBBA, says MIT study
articles.summary: 74% of all new clean electricity capacity that would have been added under the Inflation Reduction Act will be preserved despite Trump administration policy changes, the report estimates, including 82% of utility-scale solar generation.

articles.title: New Jersey increases transmission oversight in ‘affordability’ push
articles.summary: New Jersey’s governor signed bills that aim to cut transmission owners’ return on equity, establish data center tariffs and require state approval for “supplementary” transmission projects.

articles.title: India inaugurates nuclear-powered hydrogen production facility
articles.summary: The facility uses process heat from the Fast Breeder Test Reactor to produce hydrogen through the copper-chlorine thermochemical process developed by Indian researchers.

articles.title: Blykalla teams up with Hitachi for SMR deployment
articles.summary: Sweden's Blykalla and Hitachi Energy - the energy arm of Japan's Hitachi Group - have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore a long-term collaboration on enabling the deployment of next-generation lead-cooled advanced modular reactors.

articles.title: Polish developer applies for CfD for three SMR plants
articles.summary: Orlen Synthos Green Energy has applied to Poland's Minister of Energy for a Contract for Difference for the construction of a total of 14 BWRX-300 small modular reactors at three locations in Poland.

articles.title: First Nations group takes stake in Ontario nuclear plant
articles.summary: The Williams Treaties First Nations is investing CAD700 million (USD492 million) in Ontario Power Generation's project to build a BWRX-300 reactor - the Darlington New Nuclear Project - with the support of loan guarantees from federal and provincial programmes.

articles.title: In pictures: Akkuyu 2's inner dome lifted into place
articles.summary: The inner containment dome has been lifted into place at the second unit of Turkey's first nuclear power plant.

articles.title: Fuel loading begins at Slovakia's Mochovce 4
articles.summary: Slovenské elektrárne has begun loading nuclear fuel into Mochovce Nuclear Power Plant's fourth unit, marking the start of its active commissioning.

articles.title: Scottish sites suitable for nuclear new build, study says
articles.summary: Scotland has areas with "high potential" for new nuclear development from a technical perspective, according to a new siting study by Great British Energy - Nuclear, the UK government's nuclear delivery body.

articles.title: State support needed to make new Swiss reactors viable, report says
articles.summary: The construction of new nuclear power reactors in Switzerland is not competitive under current conditions, but would become profitable with state subsidies, risk mitigation and significantly lower construction costs, according to a study from ETH Zurich and the Paul Scherrer Institute.

articles.title: In pictures: Final module installed at Haiyang 4
articles.summary: The last large module - the CB20 containment water tank module - has been installed at unit 4 of the Haiyang nuclear power plant site in China's Shandong province, State Power Investment Corporation announced.

articles.title: Criticality for third US reactor ahead of 4 July deadline
articles.summary: Deployable Energy's Unity demonstration reactor has successfully achieved initial criticality at the National Reactor Innovation Center located at Idaho National Laboratory - which means the US has achieved the presidential goal set last year of three microreactors under Department of Energy authorisation to achieve initial

articles.title: SGE-led team targets 14 BWRX-300 SMRs in UK
articles.summary: Poland's SGE and a deployment team including Samsung C&T, Laing O'Rourke, Aecon Group and Google Cloud, have outlined plans for the privately financed deployment of 14 GE Vernova Hitachi BWRX-300 small modular reactors across three sites in the UK.

articles.title: TRISO fuel delivered for Kaleidos reactor experiment
articles.summary: The first shipment of fuel for full-power, full-temperature testing of Radiant's Kaleidos microreactor technology has been delivered to the National Reactor Innovation Center's Demonstration of Microreactor Experiments facility at Idaho National Laboratory.

articles.title: Fuel loading completed at Mochovce 4
articles.summary: Slovenské elektrárne has announced that all 349 nuclear fuel assemblies have been successfully loaded into Mochovce 4. The process took five days, and was completed on Friday 3 July.

articles.title: Second Taipingling unit begins supplying power
articles.summary: Unit 2 of the Taipingling nuclear power plant has begun supplying electricity to the grid for the first time, China General Nuclear announced. The unit is the second of six Hualong One (HPR1000) reactors planned for the site in Guangdong province.

articles.title: Ampera says it has 3D-printed microreactor module
articles.summary: US-based Ampera Inc says it has achieved what it calls a major milestone by completing the production of the first full-scale, 3D-printed nuclear reactor module.

articles.title: Control room simulator launched for lead-cooled BREST-OD-300 reactor
articles.summary: A full-scale simulator of the control room for the lead-cooled fast neutron BREST-OD-300 reactor has been commissioned, allowing training for staff before the unit's future physical startup.

articles.title: Agreement could see prototype microreactor built at Berkeley
articles.summary: Chiltern Vital Group has signed a letter of intent with Cambridge Atomworks to consider the construction of the prototype Odin microreactor on the Berkeley Green Science and Technology Park in Gloucestershire, England.

articles.title: Criticality for fourth US microreactor to meet 4 July deadline
articles.summary: Aalo Atomics announced that its Critical Test Reactor at the Idaho National Laboratory successfully achieved initial criticality in the early hours of Saturday morning, becoming the fourth microreactor under US Department of Energy authorisation to achieve the milestone by 4 July 2026.

articles.title: Dukovany project on schedule, says Czech ministry's progress report
articles.summary: Geotechnical surveys, including drilling more than 13 kilometres of exploratory wells, have been completed, the first conceptual design has been submitted, and several Czech suppliers selected in the year since contracts were signed for the new nuclear project at Dukovany, the Czech Ministry of Trade and Industry has reported.

articles.title: Deep Fission receives prototype reactor canister
articles.summary: California-based startup Deep Fission, which aims to place small modular reactors in boreholes a mile underground, has announced the delivery of its prototype reactor canister for its pilot project to the Parsons site in Kansas.
